dedupe_keys.name: crisisnlp crisis informatics datasets including crisismmd humaid medic and incidents1m

description: CrisisNLP is a repository of labelled social media datasets, benchmarks and tools for research on crisis response. Its 22 resources include human-labelled tweets from 19 natural and human-induced disasters sorted into humanitarian categories (such as infrastructure and utility damage, injured or dead people, rescue and donation efforts), CrisisMMD with 16,058 tweets and 18,082 images from seven 2017 disasters labelled for informativeness, humanitarian category and damage severity, the HumAID tweet set, crisis image benchmarks such as MEDIC and Incidents1M, location-mention datasets and COVID-19 tweet collections. The producer is the Crisis Computing team at the Qatar Computing Research Institute. Coverage is global and event-based, from 2011 to the 2020s: earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, wildfires and the pandemic. Files are tweet identifiers with labels, images and code, free to download, under terms of use that limit use to research on humanitarian computing. Caveats: most text resources give tweet ids, so full content must be rehydrated through the platform, which may no longer be possible; labels come from crowd annotation with disagreement; events are skewed to English and North America. Simulation uses: training and testing classifiers for situational awareness in emergency operations centres, and observed timelines of damage and needs reports to drive response exercises. Related records: xBD (data-xbd-building-damage) gives satellite damage labels.
